title: prez refuse_external is case-sensitive, whitespace-intolerant and line-bound, so three more external-reference shapes reach the artifact
body:
`refuse_external` matches literal byte sequences against single lines, but a CSS reference is a token whose spelling is case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant and newline-tolerant. Three further shapes therefore reach the artifact untouched. **Shipped in 2.8.0. Distinct from 0014 and from 0015, in root cause and in fix.**

## The defect

`crates/artifact/src/theme.rs:453-457` is the whole check:

```rust
for (number, line) in strip_comments(source).lines().enumerate() {
  let found = ["http://", "https://", "url(//", "url('//", "url(\"//"]
    .into_iter()
    .find(|needle| line.contains(needle));
```

`str::contains` is case-sensitive and the needles carry no whitespace tolerance, and `.lines()` bounds every match to one line. CSS obeys none of those three constraints:

- **Case.** `url(` and a URL scheme are both ASCII case-insensitive in CSS. `URL(//cdn/x.png)` and `url(HTTP://cdn/x.png)` match no needle.
- **Whitespace.** `url( //cdn/x.png )` is a legal url token. The needle is the literal `url(//`.
- **Line orientation.** `@import\n"//cdn/x.css";` is one legal at-rule spanning two lines. No line contains a whole needle.

**This is why 0014's fix must not be a longer needle list.** Widening the list to cover these means enumerating `url(`, `URL(`, `Url(`, `url (`, `url(\n` and the cross product with each quoting form -- a list sized to the instances someone happened to try. The requirement is a property of CSS tokens; the instrument is a substring scan; **no needle set closes that gap.**

## Measured, 13 fixtures with two controls plus two detector controls

`opt/prez/crate/target/release/prez` rebuilt from `5e86fc5` (4.42s, a real compile). Each fixture is a `--theme-file` against a two-line deck; `rc` is prez's exit; the last column asks whether the offending host fragment reached the emitted HTML, read with newlines squashed and case-insensitively.

| id | fixture                                             | rc | reached artifact | class                     |
| -- | --------------------------------------------------- | -- | ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| C1 | `body{color:#333}`                                  | 0  | no               | green control             |
| C2 | `body{background:url(https://cdn/x.png)}`           | 2  | --               | **red control -- wired**  |
| E1 | `@import "//cdn/x.css";`                            | 0  | YES              | issue 0014                |
| E2 | `@import '//cdn/x.css';`                            | 0  | YES              | issue 0014                |
| E3 | `@import url(//cdn/x.css);`                         | 2  | --               | already caught            |
| E4 | `body{background:url( //cdn/x.png )}`               | 0  | YES              | **THIS ISSUE -- space**   |
| E5 | `body{background:URL(//cdn/x.png)}`                 | 0  | YES              | **THIS ISSUE -- case**    |
| E6 | `body{background:url(HTTP://cdn/x.png)}`            | 0  | YES              | **THIS ISSUE -- case**    |
| E7 | `body{content:"/*"}` then `@import "https://..."`   | 0  | YES              | issue 0015                |
| E8 | `/* oops` unterminated then `@import "https://..."` | 0  | YES              | issue 0015                |
| E9 | `@import` NEWLINE `"//cdn/x.css";`                  | 0  | YES              | **THIS ISSUE -- lines**   |
| F1 | `body{content:"//"}`                                | 0  | no               | false-positive control    |
| F2 | `/* see http://example.com */`                      | 0  | YES              | false-positive control    |

Nine of thirteen escape and every one of the nine ships its reference. F2's YES is correct: a comment reaches the artifact and fetches nothing, and it is here as the detector's presence arm.

## The detector reproduced the defect it was measuring, and that is the finding under the finding

The first run of this probe read the artifact with `grep -E 'url\([^)]*//|HTTP://'`, line-oriented and case-sensitive. It reported E5 and E9 as **not reaching the artifact**, which is exactly the wrong answer, for exactly the two reasons the code under test is wrong. **A case-blind instrument measuring a case-blind defect returns a clean result.** Both were caught only because the second detector -- flatten newlines, match case-insensitively, key on the host fragment rather than on the reference's shape -- disagreed with the first. Neither run errored.

## Severity

Medium, matching 0014 and 0015: same guarantee, same reach, same absence of any warning. `help/prez.md` sells an artifact that "opens offline, from a USB stick, from an email attachment, in five years"; each of E4, E5, E6 and E9 makes that false silently.

## Why it is filed rather than folded into ST0017

hv's 2026-07-29 precedent, the same one 0014 and 0015 were filed under: a defect that shipped earns an issue even when the fix lands inside a steel thread. The fix lands in ST0017/WP-03 with 0014's and 0015's, under AC-3.5, and R2's ruling already names the correct rule -- *protocol-relative in `url(...)` and in `@import`, not in arbitrary string content*. **What this issue adds is that no needle list can implement that ruling.**
